Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reference run + resilience scenarios for Redwood connector

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. BlueHarbor's architecture team would like to run a focused validation on the Redwood connector reference architecture before we commit to the Dedicated deployment. Specifically we want to: 
- Verify failover/fallback behavior across model variants and regions
- Exercise high-concurrency prefix caching scenarios (bursts to 500 QPS for short windows)
- Confirm network peering and egress patterns for our VPC-to-Redwood Private option

Can your team help define a short validation plan (2–3 days of tests) and run a runbook walkthrough? We can provide a staging workload and a sample corpus.

Available windows for our engineering team: Thu 4/16 (PST afternoon) or Mon 4/20 (PST morning).

I've attached our current network diagram and a short note on expected peak profiles.

Attachments: blueharbor-network-diagram.pdf

Regards,
Kelly Turner
CTO, BlueHarbor Consulting
kelly@blueharbor.io
+1 415-555-0134

Hi Kelly — thanks for this and the diagram. We can definitely run a compact validation and a runbook walkthrough. Proposed plan high-level: 
1) Day 0 (prep): exchange staging creds, confirm network routes + token-handling.
2) Day 1 (functional): smoke tests for model variant routing and auth, baseline latency/cost.
3) Day 2 (resilience): controlled burst tests, region failover, KV/prefix cache warm/cold experiments.

A few asks to help scope:
- Can you share sampling of request sizes (avg tokens in/out) and burst window durations?
- Are you planning to use Dedicated or Private (VPC) for the initial run?
- Any compliance constraints (storage/retention) we should mirror in the staging environment?

We can meet Thu 4/16 at 2:30pm PST for the walkthrough — tentative invite to follow. Marissa, Sergio — can you own the resilience test plan and runbook updates (RB-4821)?

Best,
Rishi
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Apr 14, 2026 at 11:03 AM rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai wrote:
> Hi Kelly — thanks for this and the diagram. We can definitely run a compact validation and a runbook walkthrough.

Thanks Rishi — attaching the token profile and a short traffic extract from our runners. Quick answers inline: 
- Typical request size: 120 tokens in / 150 tokens out average; 95th token size ~600 tokens for batch summarization jobs.
- Burst windows: realistic spikes of 300–500 QPS for ~30–90s during user spikes; steady-state 25–40 QPS.
- We'll start with Private (VPC) pilot but can accept sandboxed Dedicated variants if that simplifies routing.
- Compliance: SOC2 in process, but primary concern for the run is egress logging and auditability.

Attachments: blueharbor-workload-sample.json, blueharbor-network-diagram.pdf

Kelly

Thanks — attaching the resilience test plan and the runbook diff for the BlueHarbor pilot. Highlights:
- Day 1: routing/variant smoke tests (pass = no more than 5% error rate, median latency < 180ms for baseline model)
- Day 2: resilience exercises: region failover (cut region A), cache cold-start burst (500 QPS for 60s), quantization fallback test (switch to smaller quantized variant under pressure)
- Rollback: automatic routing fallback to hosted-compatible variant + alerting to on-call if error rate > 7% for >2 mins

Attachments: resilience-test-plan.xlsx, redwood-runbook-diff.txt

I've scheduled the walkthrough Thu 4/23 10:00am PST (we needed a few extra days to prepare infra). Kelly — please confirm that slot or propose alternate.

Marissa
